description: What a Backspace pressed after an expansion leaves on screen (hotstrings.backspace_restore_enabled, hotstrings.backspace_restore_window_ms). Replayed by the shared rule (_shared/hotstrings/engine/backspace_restore.lua) on macOS and Linux through _shared/tests/lua/hotstrings/backspace_restore_contract.lua, and by the Windows dispatcher (HSE_UndoExpansion) in tests/unit/hotstrings/engine/engine/test_backspace_undo.ahk.

field_semantics.trigger: The text the user typed for the expansion, as it was on screen, the magic key included when it ended the trigger.
field_semantics.output: The expansion's literal output, without the terminator.
field_semantics.terminator: Optional: the end character that fired the expansion. Absent for an expansion that fired on its last trigger character.
field_semantics.terminator_consumed: Optional, false when absent: the terminator selected the match but was not typed after the output.
field_semantics.elapsed_ms: Milliseconds between the expansion's commit and the Backspace.
field_semantics.key_between: Optional, false when absent: another key was pressed between the expansion and the Backspace.
field_semantics.undoes: Whether the Backspace undoes the expansion.
field_semantics.screen_after: What the expansion's part of the line reads after the Backspace: the restored text when it undoes, otherwise the output and replayed terminator less their last character.

vectors.description: td★ typed td★ → 2026-08-01; Backspace gives td, not td★.
btw then ★ as a consumed terminator → by the way; Backspace gives btw.
The repeat key's trigger is the lone magic key: po★ → poo, Backspace gives po.
adn then Space → ADN and Space; Backspace gives adn and Space, not ADN and Space.
adn then a comma → ADN,; Backspace gives adn,.
adn then Enter → ADN and a new line; Backspace gives adn and the new line.
A case-conformed trigger comes back as typed: Adn then Space → Adn and Space.
The window is inclusive: a Backspace exactly at its end still undoes.
One millisecond past the window the Backspace deletes the Space.
Past the window a magic-key expansion loses its last character like any text.
A two-second window undoes a Backspace one second after the expansion.
With hotstrings.backspace_restore_enabled off the Backspace is a plain Backspace.
Off, a magic-key expansion is not undone either.
Escape, or any other key, pressed after the expansion ends the undo chance: the Backspace then deletes the Space.
